To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

PNCC features are superior to RASTA PLPs in terms of speaker recognition performance and that GMM based system performs better than i-Vector based system for short utterance and the i-Vector based SR system is better for longer utterances.
PNCC and Rasta PLP are both suitable for speaker recognition, but the performance of the system is better with PNCC than Rasta PLP
PNCC features are more effective for short utterances whereas i-vector method is more suitable for longer utterances.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the comparison of performance of GMM and i-vector method for SR with PNCC and PLP features.
the comparison of the performance of speaker recognition systems implemented using two different methods and two different features.
the performance of speaker verification system using GMM and I-vector methods with PNCC features.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
i-vector method with PNCC features is better for longer utterances and GMM method with PNCC is better for shorter utterances.
GMM and i-vector based SR systems perform better when PNCC features are used.
GMM and i-vector based SR systems with PNCC features are better than RASTA-PLP based SR systems.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
i-vector method with PNCC features provides a better performance for longer utterances and GMM method with RASTA PLPs provides a better performance with shorter utterances.
for short utterances, GMM based system performs better than i-Vector system and for long utterances, i-vector method performs better than GMM.
for short utterances, GMM is a better choice and for longer utterances, i-Vector with PLDA is better.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the performance of the SR system depends on various factors like type of features used, length of the utterance, number of training utterances, and the classifier used.
the choice of feature extraction method and classification technique should be made depending on the type of application.
the performance of i-Vector based speaker recognition systems can be improved significantly by using a better feature extraction technique.
